itens.s: Writing the right query and understanding why it is slow.
itens.k: sql language writing the right query and understanding why it is slow. before administering any database you need to talk to it. joins, aggregation, subqueries and window functions are the vocabulary; reading an execution plan is the grammar.

itens.s: Memory, processes, transaction log and persistence.
itens.k: database architecture memory, processes, transaction log and persistence. what happens between commit and the data on disk. buffer pool, redo/wal, checkpoint, undo/mvcc. without this, every diagnosis is a guess.

itens.s: RPO and RTO you have actually tested.
itens.k: backup & recovery rpo and rto you have actually tested. strategy, retention, duplexing, pitr and — above all — restore testing. a backup never restored is a promise, not a guarantee.
performance evidence-based diagnosis, not guesswork. wait events, plans, statistics and instrumentation. finding out where the time went before touching anything.

itens.s: The same data in more than one place, consistently.
itens.k: replication the same data in more than one place, consistently. binlog and gtid, wal streaming, always on, goldengate. sync and async modes, lag, replica rebuilds and conflict resolution.

itens.s: Surviving the loss of a node with no human intervention.
itens.k: high availability surviving the loss of a node with no human intervention. rac, data guard, innodb cluster, patroni, always on. quorum, fencing, split-brain and automatic failover — and the cost of each guarantee.

itens.s: Encryption, least privilege and an auditable trail.
itens.k: security encryption, least privilege and an auditable trail. tde, tls, rbac, masking, separation of duties and auditing that survives a compliance inspection.

itens.s: Understanding what the provider takes on — and what stays yours.
itens.k: cloud understanding what the provider takes on — and what stays yours. managed services on oci, aws, azure and gcp. shared-responsibility model, real sla, cost and the limitations the console does not show.

itens.s: Stop operating by hand and start versioning change.
itens.k: automation & dbre stop operating by hand and start versioning change. infrastructure as code, schema pipelines, observability with slos and chaos testing. the database treated as part of engineering, not as a black box.

itens.s: Deciding architecture and owning the trade-off.
itens.k: senior dba deciding architecture and owning the trade-off. it is not about knowing everything — it is about knowing what to ask, measuring the risk and defending the choice with data. career, positioning and certification come in here as a consequence, not as the goal.
